To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the AR NTD and LBD interact in a ligand-dependent manner, that this interaction is mediated by a PhixxPhixPhi motif in the AR NTD, and that this motif is embedded in a longer amphipathic helix that is essential for N/C interaction.
amino acids 3-12 in AR3-13 contribute to the transactivation activity of the NTD-AR.LDB complex, and that amino acids in and around the PhixxPhiΦ motif, 23FXXLF27, modulate the N/C interaction.

AR3-13 is required for AR transactivation function, that AR16-36 is required for AR LBD interaction and that amino acids in and around the 23FixLF27 motif modulates the interaction between the AR NTD and the AR LBD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the N/C interaction and the functional significance of the PhixxPhi motif in the AR.
the structural and functional characterization of AR16-36 and its role in N/C interaction.
the identification of functional domains and residues in AR3-13 as well as AR16-36 that contribute to LBD interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PhixxPhi motif 23FxxL27 is essential for the N/C interaction, whereas the flanking amino acids are important for fine-tuning of the interaction.
the PhixxPhi motif in AR16-36 is a protein interaction motif that modulates the interaction between the androgen receptor N-terminal and liganded ligand-binding domains.

the 23FXXLF27 motif in AR16-36 plays a dominant role in the LBD interaction, but the flanking amino acids in AR3-13, and in and flanking 23FxxFL27, modulate the N/C interaction in a positive or negative way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
amino acids 3-16 in the AR NTD are required for the N/C interaction.
amino acids 3-12 in AR3-13 contribute to transactivation, whereas amino acids in and surrounding the 23FxxxLF27 motif are essential for LBD association.
the 30VREV134 motif in AR3 36 is not a protein interaction motif.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AR NTD is a complex protein domain that can be subdivided in functionally distinct fragments, each of which contributes to the N/C interaction.
the AR NTD can be divided into two functionally different fragments.
the 23FxxxLF27 motif is not a simple protein interaction motif but that it has to be considered in a broader context of the surrounding amino acid residues.
